name_translation: The Yoga of the Vision of the Universal Form

verses.speaker: अर्जुन उवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
मदनुग्रहाय परमं गुह्यमध्यात्मसंज्ञितम् |
यत्त्वयोक्तं वचस्तेन मोहोऽयं vigato mama || १ ||
verses.sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
मदनुग्रहाय परमं गुह्यमध्यात्मसंज्ञितम् |
यत्त्वयोक्तं वचस्तेन मोहोऽयं विगतो मम || १ ||
verses.transliteration:
arjuna uvāca |
madanugrahāya paramaṃ guhyamadhyātmasaṃjñitam |
yattvayoktaṃ vacastena moho'yaṃ vigato mama || 1 ||
verses.word_meanings: arjunaḥ uvāca—Arjuna said; mat-anugrahāya—out of compassion for me; paramam—supreme; guhyam—confidential; adhyātma-saṃjñitam—concerning the nature of the Supreme Self; yat—which; tvayā—by You; uktam—spoken; vacaḥ—words; tena—by that; mohaḥ ayam—this delusion of mine; vigataḥ—is dispelled; mama—my.
verses.translation: Arjuna said: By the supreme and most confidential words concerning the Self which You have spoken out of compassion for me, this delusion of mine has been dispelled.
verses.meaning: Arjuna opens Chapter 11 by expressing profound gratitude to Sri Krishna. The sublime philosophical instructions of Chapters 7 through 10 regarding the transcendent nature of God, Brahman, and divine opulences have completely eradicated Arjuna's initial confusion and grief.
verses.purport: Arjuna opens Chapter 11 by expressing profound gratitude to Sri Krishna. The sublime philosophical instructions of Chapters 7 through 10 regarding the transcendent nature of God, Brahman, and divine opulences have completely eradicated Arjuna's initial confusion and grief.

verses.speaker: अर्जुन उवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
भवाप्ययौ हि भूतानां श्रुतौ विस्तरशो मया |
त्वत्तः कमलपत्राक्ष माहात्म्यमपि चाव्ययम् || २ ||
verses.sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
भवाप्ययौ हि भूतानां श्रुतौ विस्तरशो मया |
त्वत्तः कमलपत्राक्ष माहात्म्यमपि चाव्ययम् || २ ||
verses.transliteration:
arjuna uvāca |
bhavāpyayau hi bhūtānāṃ śrutau vistaraśo mayā |
tvattaḥ kamalapatrākṣa māhātmyamapi cāvyayam || 2 ||
verses.word_meanings: bhava-apyayau—origin and dissolution; hi—indeed; bhūtānām—of living beings; śrutau—have been heard; vistaraśaḥ—in detail; mayā—by me; tvattaḥ—from You; kamala-patra-akṣa—O lotus-eyed one (Krishna); māhātmyam—greatness/glory; api ca—and also; avyayam—imperishable.
verses.translation: The origin and dissolution of all beings have been heard by me in detail from You, O lotus-eyed Lord, as well as Your inexhaustible, imperishable greatness.
verses.meaning: Arjuna lovingly addresses Sri Krishna as 'Kamala-patraksha' (the lotus-eyed one) and acknowledges having heard the vast cosmic mechanics of creation, maintenance, and dissolution along with Krishna's eternal sovereignty.
verses.purport: Arjuna lovingly addresses Sri Krishna as 'Kamala-patraksha' (the lotus-eyed one) and acknowledges having heard the vast cosmic mechanics of creation, maintenance, and dissolution along with Krishna's eternal sovereignty.

verses.speaker: अर्जुन उवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
एवमेतद्यथात्थ त्वमात्मानं परमेश्वर |
द्रष्टुमिच्छामि ते रूपमैश्वरं पुरुषोत्तम || ३ ||
verses.sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
एवमेतद्यथात्थ त्वमात्मानं परमेश्वर |
द्रष्टुमिच्छामि ते रूपमैश्वरं पुरुषोत्तम || ३ ||
verses.transliteration:
arjuna uvāca |
evametadyathāttha tvamātmānaṃ parameśvara |
draṣṭumicchāmi te rūpamaiśvaraṃ puruṣottama || 3 ||
verses.word_meanings: evam etat—it is so; yathā—as; āttha—have declared; tvam—You; ātmānam—Yourself; parama-īśvara—O Supreme Lord; draṣṭum icchāmi—I desire to see; te—Your; rūpam aiśvaram—sovereign cosmic form; puruṣa-uttama—O Supreme Person.
verses.translation: O Supreme Lord, as You have described Yourself to be, even so is it. Yet I desire to behold with my own eyes Your sovereign, cosmic divine form (Rupam Aishvaram), O Supreme Person!
verses.meaning: Arjuna fully believes the words of Sri Krishna without doubt; his request to behold the Universal Form (Vishvarupa) is not born of skepticism, but of deep reverence and a desire to see God's all-encompassing cosmic reality unveiled for the benefit of all humanity.
verses.purport: Arjuna fully believes the words of Sri Krishna without doubt; his request to behold the Universal Form (Vishvarupa) is not born of skepticism, but of deep reverence and a desire to see God's all-encompassing cosmic reality unveiled for the benefit of all humanity.

verses.speaker: अर्जुन उवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
मन्यसे यदि तच्छक्यं मया द्रष्टुमिति प्रभो |
योगेश्वर ततो मे त्वं दर्शयात्मानमव्ययम् || ४ ||
verses.sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
मन्यसे यदि तच्छक्यं मया द्रष्टुमिति प्रभो |
योगेश्वर ततो मे त्वं दर्शयात्मानमव्ययम् || ४ ||
verses.transliteration:
arjuna uvāca |
manyase yadi tacchakyaṃ mayā draṣṭumiti prabho |
yogeśvara tato me tvaṃ darśayātmānamavyayam || 4 ||
verses.word_meanings: manyase—You think; yadi—if; tat—that; śakyam—is possible; mayā—by me; draṣṭum—to be seen; iti—thus; prabho—O Lord; yoga-īśvara—O Lord of Yoga; tataḥ—then; me—unto me; tvam—You; darśaya—reveal; ātmānam—Your Self; avyayam—the imperishable.
verses.translation: If You think, O Lord, that it is possible for me to behold it, then, O Master of all Yoga (Yogeshvara), please reveal to me Your imperishable Universal Self!
verses.meaning: Arjuna exemplifies ideal humility in spiritual inquiry: He does not demand or presume entitlement to witness the Cosmic Form, but places himself entirely at the grace and discretion of the Lord of Yoga (Yogeshvara).
verses.purport: Arjuna exemplifies ideal humility in spiritual inquiry: He does not demand or presume entitlement to witness the Cosmic Form, but places himself entirely at the grace and discretion of the Lord of Yoga (Yogeshvara).

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
पश्य मे पार्थ रूपाणि शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः |
नानाविधानि दिव्यानि नानावर्णाकृतीनि च || ५ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
पश्य मे पार्थ रूपाणि शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः |
नानाविधानि दिव्यानि नानावर्णाकृतीनि च || ५ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
paśya me pārtha rūpāṇi śataśo'tha sahasraśaḥ |
nānāvidhāni divyāni nānāvarṇākṛtīni ca || 5 ||
verses.word_meanings: śrī-bhagavān uvāca—the Supreme Lord said; paśya—behold; me—My; pārtha—O son of Pritha; rūpāṇi—forms; śataśaḥ—by hundreds; atha—and; sahasraśaḥ—by thousands; nānā-vidhāni—manifold/multifarious; divyāni—divine; nānā-varṇa-ākṛtīni—of various colors and shapes; ca—and.
verses.translation: The Supreme Lord said: Behold, O Partha, My divine forms by the hundreds and thousands, of manifold varieties, colors, and shapes!
verses.meaning: Sri Krishna grants Arjuna's prayer and invites him to look into the infinite tapestry of divine manifestations—countless celestial embodiments pulsating with transcendental colors, geometries, and powers.
verses.purport: Sri Krishna grants Arjuna's prayer and invites him to look into the infinite tapestry of divine manifestations—countless celestial embodiments pulsating with transcendental colors, geometries, and powers.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
पश्यादित्यान्वसून्रुद्रानश्विनौ मरुतस्तथा |
बहून्यदृष्टपूर्वाणि पश्याश्चर्याणि भारत || ६ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
पश्यादित्यान्वसून्रुद्रानश्विनौ मरुतस्तथा |
बहून्यदृष्टपूर्वाणि पश्याश्चर्याणि भारत || ६ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
paśyādityānvasūnrudrānaśvinau marutastathā |
bahūnyadṛṣṭapūrvāṇi paśyāścaryāṇi bhārata || 6 ||
verses.word_meanings: paśya—behold; ādityān—the twelve Adityas; vasūn—the eight Vasus; rudrān—the eleven Rudras; aśvinau—the twin Ashvins; marutaḥ tathā—and the Maruts (wind deities); bahūni—many; adṛṣṭa-pūrvāṇi—never seen before; paśya—behold; āścaryāṇi—wondrous sights; bhārata—O descendant of Bharata.
verses.translation: Behold the Adityas, the Vasus, the Rudras, the twin Ashvins, and the Maruts! Behold, O Bharata, countless wondrous sights never before witnessed by mortal eyes!
verses.meaning: The entire Vedic pantheon of cosmic hierarchies is revealed within Sri Krishna's body, along with marvels and cosmic vistas that no mortal had ever before experienced.
verses.purport: The entire Vedic pantheon of cosmic hierarchies is revealed within Sri Krishna's body, along with marvels and cosmic vistas that no mortal had ever before experienced.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
इहैकस्थं जगत्कृत्स्नं पश्याद्य सचराचरम् |
मम देहे गुडाकेश यच्चान्यद्द्रष्टुमिच्छसि || ७ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
इहैकस्थं जगत्कृत्स्नं पश्याद्य सचराचरम् |
मम देहे गुडाकेश यच्चान्यद्द्रष्टुमिच्छसि || ७ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
ihaikasthaṃ jagatkṛtsnaṃ paśyādya sacarācaram |
mama dehe guḍākeśa yaccānyaddraṣṭumicchasi || 7 ||
verses.word_meanings: iha—here; eka-stham—standing unified in one place; jagat kṛtsnam—the entire universe; paśya—behold; adya—today/now; sa-cara-acaram—moving and unmoving; mama dehe—in My body; guḍākeśa—O Gudakesha (Arjuna); yat ca—and whatever; anyat—else; draṣṭum icchasi—you wish to see.
verses.translation: Behold now, O Gudakesha, standing concentrated in one place within My divine body, the entire universe with all its moving and unmoving beings, and whatever else you desire to see!
verses.meaning: The entire spacetime continuum, past, present, and future, all galaxies, dimensions, and outcomes of the impending Kurukshetra war are concentrated within the single divine frame of Sri Krishna.
verses.purport: The entire spacetime continuum, past, present, and future, all galaxies, dimensions, and outcomes of the impending Kurukshetra war are concentrated within the single divine frame of Sri Krishna.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
न तु मां शक्यसे द्रष्टुमनेनैव स्वचक्षुषा |
दिव्यं ददामि ते चक्षुः पश्य मे योगमैश्वरम् || ८ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
न तु मां शक्यसे द्रष्टुमनेनैव स्वचक्षुषा |
दिव्यं ददामि ते चक्षुः पश्य मे योगमैश्वरम् || ८ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
na tu māṃ śakyase draṣṭumanenaiva svacakṣuṣā |
divyaṃ dadāmi te cakṣuḥ paśya me yogamaiśvaram || 8 ||
verses.word_meanings: na tu—not however; mām—Me; śakyase—you are able; draṣṭum—to see; anena eva—with these indeed; sva-cakṣuṣā—with your physical eyes; divyam—divine; dadāmi—I bestow; te—unto you; cakṣuḥ—vision/eye; paśya—behold; me—My; yogam aiśvaram—sovereign divine mystic power.
verses.translation: But you cannot behold Me with your physical eyes. Therefore, I bestow upon you divine spiritual vision (Divya Chakshu); behold now My sovereign divine power (Yogam Aishvaram)!
verses.meaning: A monumental verse: Material physical senses are limited to physical wavelengths and finite forms. To perceive the infinite, multidimensional reality of the Absolute, one requires the grace of Divya Chakshu—spiritual intuition and divine vision bestowed directly by the Lord.
verses.purport: A monumental verse: Material physical senses are limited to physical wavelengths and finite forms. To perceive the infinite, multidimensional reality of the Absolute, one requires the grace of Divya Chakshu—spiritual intuition and divine vision bestowed directly by the Lord.

verses.speaker: सञ्जय उवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
सञ्जय उवाच |
एवमुक्त्वा ततो राजन्महायोगेश्वरो हरिः |
दर्शयामास पार्थाय परमं रूपमैश्वरम् || ९ ||
verses.sanskrit:
सञ्जय उवाच |
एवमुक्त्वा ततो राजन्महायोगेश्वरो हरिः |
दर्शयामास पार्थाय परमं रूपमैश्वरम् || ९ ||
verses.transliteration:
sañjaya uvāca |
evamuktvā tato rājanmahāyogeśvaro hariḥ |
darśayāmāsa pārthāya paramaṃ rūpamaiśvaram || 9 ||
verses.word_meanings: sañjayaḥ uvāca—Sanjaya said; evam uktvā—having spoken thus; tataḥ—then; rājan—O King (Dhritarashtra); mahā-yoga-īśvaraḥ—the Great Lord of Yoga; hariḥ—Sri Hari (Krishna); darśayāmāsa—revealed; pārthāya—unto the son of Pritha (Arjuna); paramam—the supreme; rūpam aiśvaram—sovereign cosmic form.
verses.translation: Sanjaya said: Having spoken thus, O King, the Great Lord of all Yoga, Sri Hari, revealed to Partha His supreme, sovereign cosmic form.
verses.meaning: Sanjaya, gifted with clairvoyant spiritual vision by sage Vyasa, describes to the blind King Dhritarashtra the breathtaking moment when Sri Krishna manifested the supreme Vishvarupa to Arjuna.
verses.purport: Sanjaya, gifted with clairvoyant spiritual vision by sage Vyasa, describes to the blind King Dhritarashtra the breathtaking moment when Sri Krishna manifested the supreme Vishvarupa to Arjuna.

verses.speaker: सञ्जय उवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
सञ्जय उवाच |
अनेकवक्त्रनयनमनेकाद्भुतदर्शनम् |
अनेकदिव्याभरणं दिव्यानेकोद्यतायुधम् || १० ||
verses.sanskrit:
सञ्जय उवाच |
अनेकवक्त्रनयनमनेकाद्भुतदर्शनम् |
अनेकदिव्याभरणं दिव्यानेकोद्यतायुधम् || १० ||
verses.transliteration:
sañjaya uvāca |
anekavaktranayanamanekādbhutadarśanam |
anekadivyābharaṇaṃ divyānekodyatāyudham || 10 ||
verses.word_meanings: aneka-vaktra-nayanam—with manifold mouths and eyes; aneka-adbhuta-darśanam—with countless wondrous sights; aneka-divya-ābharaṇam—adorned with many celestial ornaments; divya-aneka-udyata-āyudham—holding numerous raised divine weapons.
verses.translation: Having countless mouths and eyes, displaying manifold wondrous sights, adorned with numerous celestial ornaments, and brandishing many uplifted divine weapons;
verses.meaning: The Vishvarupa appears with infinite perspectives—innumerable seeing eyes, speaking mouths, resplendent celestial jewels, and dazzling cosmic weaponry held aloft.
verses.purport: The Vishvarupa appears with infinite perspectives—innumerable seeing eyes, speaking mouths, resplendent celestial jewels, and dazzling cosmic weaponry held aloft.

verses.speaker: सञ्जय उवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
सञ्जय उवाच |
दिव्यमाल्याम्बरधरं दिव्यगन्धानुलेपनम् |
सर्वाश्चर्यमयं देवमनन्तं विश्वतोमुखम् || ११ ||
verses.sanskrit:
सञ्जय उवाच |
दिव्यमाल्याम्बरधरं दिव्यगन्धानुलेपनम् |
सर्वाश्चर्यमयं देवमनन्तं विश्वतोमुखम् || ११ ||
verses.transliteration:
sañjaya uvāca |
divyamālyāmbaradharaṃ divyagandhānulepanam |
sarvāścaryamayaṃ devamanantaṃ viśvatomukham || 11 ||
verses.word_meanings: divya-mālya-ambara-dharam—wearing celestial garlands and garments; divya-gandha-anulepanam—anointed with heavenly fragrances; sarva-āścarya-mayam—all-wonderful; devam—the radiant Lord; anantam—boundless/infinite; viśvataḥ-mukham—facing in all directions.
verses.translation: Wearing celestial garlands and divine robes, anointed with heavenly fragrances, all-wondrous, resplendent, boundless, and facing in every direction.
verses.meaning: The Cosmic Vision is not a localized object in front of the viewer; it encompasses every direction of space simultaneously, suffused with celestial fragrance and transcendental beauty.
verses.purport: The Cosmic Vision is not a localized object in front of the viewer; it encompasses every direction of space simultaneously, suffused with celestial fragrance and transcendental beauty.

verses.speaker: सञ्जय उवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
सञ्जय उवाच |
दिवि सूर्यसहस्रस्य भवेद्युगपदुत्थिता |
यदि भाः सदृशी सा स्याद्भासस्तस्य महात्मनः || १२ ||
verses.sanskrit:
सञ्जय उवाच |
दिवि सूर्यसहस्रस्य भवेद्युगपदुत्थिता |
यदि भाः सदृशी सा स्याद्भासस्तस्य महात्मनः || १२ ||
verses.transliteration:
sañjaya uvāca |
divi sūryasahasrasya bhavedyugapadutthitā |
yadi bhāḥ sadṛśī sā syādbhāsastasya mahātmanaḥ || 12 ||
verses.word_meanings: divi—in the sky; sūrya-sahasrasya—of a thousand suns; bhavet—were; yugapat—simultaneously; utthitā—blazing forth; yadi—if; bhāḥ—the effulgence; sadṛśī—comparable; sā syāt—that might be; bhāsaḥ—to the splendor; tasya mahātmanaḥ—of that Supreme Great Soul.
verses.translation: If the effulgence of a thousand suns were to blaze forth simultaneously in the sky, that might resemble the radiant splendor of that Supreme Soul!
verses.meaning: One of the most famous verses in world literature (famously recalled by J. Robert Oppenheimer at Trinity). Human language struggles to depict the intensity of divine effulgence: even a thousand suns blazing at once in the noon sky cannot fully convey the brilliance of the Lord's Cosmic Form.
