verses.speaker: सञ्जय उवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
सञ्जय उवाच |
तत्रैकस्थं जगत्कृत्स्नं प्रविभक्तमनेकधा |
अपश्यद्देवदेवस्य शरीरे पाण्डवस्तदा || १३ ||
verses.sanskrit:
सञ्जय उवाच |
तत्रैकस्थं जगत्कृत्स्नं प्रविभक्तमनेकधा |
अपश्यद्देवदेवस्य शरीरे पाण्डवस्तदा || १३ ||
verses.transliteration:
sañjaya uvāca |
tatraikasthaṃ jagatkṛtsnaṃ pravibhaktamanekadhā |
apaśyaddevadevasya śarīre pāṇḍavastadā || 13 ||
verses.word_meanings: tatra—there; eka-stham—standing in one place; jagat kṛtsnam—the entire universe; pravibhaktam—divided; anekadhā—into manifold parts; apaśyat—beheld; deva-devasya—of the God of gods; śarīre—in the body; pāṇḍavaḥ—the son of Pandu (Arjuna); tadā—then.
verses.translation: There, resting in one unified place within the body of the God of gods, the son of Pandu (Arjuna) beheld the entire universe in all its manifold divisions.
verses.meaning: Arjuna witnessed the entire multiplicity of cosmic existence—all stars, planets, dimensions, species, and historical eras—integrated in unbroken oneness within Sri Krishna's body.
verses.purport: Arjuna witnessed the entire multiplicity of cosmic existence—all stars, planets, dimensions, species, and historical eras—integrated in unbroken oneness within Sri Krishna's body.

verses.speaker: सञ्जय उवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
सञ्जय उवाच |
ततः स विस्मयाविष्टो हृष्टरोमा धनञ्जयः |
प्रणम्य शिरसा देवं कृताञ्जलिरभाषत || १४ ||
verses.sanskrit:
सञ्जय उवाच |
ततः स विस्मयाविष्टो हृष्टरोमा धनञ्जयः |
प्रणम्य शिरसा देवं कृताञ्जलिरभाषत || १४ ||
verses.transliteration:
sañjaya uvāca |
tataḥ sa vismayāviṣṭo hṛṣṭaromā dhanañjayaḥ |
praṇamya śirasā devaṃ kṛtāñjalirabhāṣata || 14 ||
verses.word_meanings: tataḥ—then; saḥ—he; vismaya-āviṣṭaḥ—filled with awe and wonder; hṛṣṭa-romā—with bodily hairs standing on end in ecstasy/terror; dhanañjayaḥ—Dhananjaya (Arjuna); praṇamya—bowing down; śirasā—with his head; devam—unto the Lord; kṛta-añjaliḥ—with folded hands; abhāṣata—began to speak.
verses.translation: Then, filled with awe and wonder, his bodily hair standing on end, Dhananjaya (Arjuna) bowed his head in reverence before the Lord, and with folded hands, began to speak.
verses.meaning: Overcome with ecstatic awe and trembling reverence (Hrishta-roma), the great warrior Arjuna casts aside all familiarity, bows low to the earth, and speaks in trembling devotion.
verses.purport: Overcome with ecstatic awe and trembling reverence (Hrishta-roma), the great warrior Arjuna casts aside all familiarity, bows low to the earth, and speaks in trembling devotion.

verses.speaker: अर्जुन उवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
पश्यामि देवांस्तव देव देहे
सर्वांस्तथा भूतविशेषसङ्घान् |
ब्रह्माणमीशं कमलासनस्थ-
मृषींश्च सर्वानुरगांश्च दिव्यान् || १५ ||
verses.sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
पश्यामि देवांस्तव देव देहे
सर्वांस्तथा भूतविशेषसङ्घान् |
ब्रह्माणमीशं कमलासनस्थ-
मृषींश्च सर्वानुरगांश्च दिव्यान् || १५ ||
verses.transliteration:
arjuna uvāca |
paśyāmi devāṃstava deva dehe
sarvāṃstathā bhūtaviśeṣasaṅghān |
brahmāṇamīśaṃ kamalāsanastha-
mṛṣīṃśca sarvānuragāṃśca divyān || 15 ||
verses.word_meanings: arjunaḥ uvāca—Arjuna said; paśyāmi—I see; devān—the gods; tava—Your; deva—O Lord; dehe—in the body; sarvān—all; tathā—also; bhūta-viśeṣa-saṅghān—hosts of diverse living beings; brahmāṇam—Brahma; īśam—Lord Shiva; kamala-āsana-stham—seated upon the lotus throne; ṛṣīn ca—and the sages; sarvān—all; uragān ca—and serpents; divyān—divine/celestial.
verses.translation: Arjuna said: O Lord, in Your body I see all the gods and the hosts of diverse beings; I see Lord Brahma seated upon his lotus throne, Lord Shiva, all the great sages, and the divine celestial serpents!
verses.meaning: Arjuna describes what he sees: The primeval Creator Brahma, the Lord of dissolution Shiva, enlightened rishis, and cosmic celestial nagas all abide within Krishna's body.
verses.purport: Arjuna describes what he sees: The primeval Creator Brahma, the Lord of dissolution Shiva, enlightened rishis, and cosmic celestial nagas all abide within Krishna's body.

verses.speaker: अर्जुन उवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
अनेकबाहूदरवक्त्रनेत्रं
पश्यामि त्वां सर्वतोऽनन्तरूपम् |
नान्तं न मध्यं न पुनस्तवादिं
पश्यामि विश्वेश्वर विश्वरूप || १६ ||
verses.sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
अनेकबाहूदरवक्त्रनेत्रं
पश्यामि त्वां सर्वतोऽनन्तरूपम् |
नान्तं न मध्यं न पुनस्तवादिं
पश्यामि विश्वेश्वर विश्वरूप || १६ ||
verses.transliteration:
arjuna uvāca |
anekabāhūdaravaktranetraṃ
paśyāmi tvāṃ sarvato'nantarūpam |
nāntaṃ na madhyaṃ na punastavādiṃ
paśyāmi viśveśvara viśvarūpa || 16 ||
verses.word_meanings: aneka-bāhu-udara-vaktra-netram—with countless arms, bellies, mouths, and eyes; paśyāmi—I see; tvām—You; sarvataḥ—everywhere; ananta-rūpam—of boundless form; na antam—neither end; na madhyam—nor middle; na punaḥ—nor again; tava—Your; ādim—origin/beginning; paśyāmi—do I see; viśva-īśvara—O Lord of the universe; viśva-rūpa—O Universal Form.
verses.translation: I see You with countless arms, bellies, mouths, and eyes, extending infinitely in every direction. O Lord of the Universe, O Universal Form, I see in You neither beginning, nor middle, nor end!
verses.meaning: The Vishvarupa is non-spatial and without temporal boundary. It cannot be framed or contained; wherever Arjuna turns his vision, infinite arms, faces, and eyes look back at him.
verses.purport: The Vishvarupa is non-spatial and without temporal boundary. It cannot be framed or contained; wherever Arjuna turns his vision, infinite arms, faces, and eyes look back at him.

verses.speaker: अर्जुन उवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
किरीटिनं गदिनं चक्रिणं च
तेजोराशिं सर्वतो दीप्तिमन्तम् |
पश्यामि त्वां दुर्निरीक्ष्यं समन्ता-
द्दीप्तानलार्कद्युतिमप्रमेयम् || १७ ||
verses.sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
किरीटिनं गदिनं चक्रिणं च
तेजोराशिं सर्वतो दीप्तिमन्तम् |
पश्यामि त्वां दुर्निरीक्ष्यं समन्ता-
द्दीप्तानलार्कद्युतिमप्रमेयम् || १७ ||
verses.transliteration:
arjuna uvāca |
kirīṭinaṃ gadinaṃ cakriṇaṃ ca
tejorāśiṃ sarvato dīptimantam |
paśyāmi tvāṃ durnirīkṣyaṃ samantā-
ddīptānalārkadyutimaprameyam || 17 ||
verses.word_meanings: kirīṭinam—with crowns; gadinam—with clubs/maces; cakriṇam ca—and with discus wheels; tejaḥ-rāśim—a mass of blazing light; sarvataḥ—on all sides; dīptimantam—radiant; paśyāmi—I behold; tvām—You; durnirīkṣyam—hard to gaze upon; samantāt—all around; dīpta-anala-arka-dyutim—with the effulgence of blazing fire and the sun; aprameyam—immeasurable.
verses.translation: I behold You adorned with diadems, holding maces and discuses, a boundless mass of light blazing everywhere, hard to look upon, dazzling like blazing fire and the blazing sun, immeasurable in every direction!
verses.meaning: The radiant majesty of the Universal Form: Countless diadems of sovereign rule, Sudarshana discuses, and maces blaze with an intensity exceeding raging fire and noonday suns.
verses.purport: The radiant majesty of the Universal Form: Countless diadems of sovereign rule, Sudarshana discuses, and maces blaze with an intensity exceeding raging fire and noonday suns.

verses.speaker: अर्जुन उवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
त्वमक्षरं परमं वेदितव्यं
त्वमस्य विश्वस्य परं निधानम् |
त्वमव्ययः शाश्वतधर्मगोप्ता
सनातनस्त्वं पुरुषो मतो मे || १८ ||
verses.sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
त्वमक्षरं परमं वेदितव्यं
त्वमस्य विश्वस्य परं निधानम् |
त्वमव्ययः शाश्वतधर्मगोप्ता
सनातनस्त्वं पुरुषो मतो मे || १८ ||
verses.transliteration:
arjuna uvāca |
tvamakṣaraṃ paramaṃ veditavyaṃ
tvamasya viśvasya paraṃ nidhānam |
tvamavyayaḥ śāśvatadharmagoptā
sanātanastvaṃ puruṣo mato me || 18 ||
verses.word_meanings: tvam—You are; akṣaram—the Imperishable; paramam—Supreme; veditavyam—that which is to be known; tvam—You are; asya viśvasya—of this universe; param nidhānam—the ultimate resting place; tvam—You are; avyayaḥ—imperishable; śāśvata-dharma-goptā—the eternal guardian of Dharma; sanātanaḥ—primeval/eternal; tvam—You are; puruṣaḥ—the Supreme Person; mataḥ me—this is my conviction.
verses.translation: You are the Imperishable Supreme Reality to be known! You are the ultimate resting place of this universe! You are the immortal Guardian of eternal Dharma, and You are the timeless Primal Person (Sanatana Purusha)—this is my firm conviction!
verses.meaning: Arjuna declares his unshakeable theological realization: Sri Krishna is the supreme knowable Absolute (Aksharam Paramam), the cosmic foundation (Param Nidhanam), and the protector of Sanatana Dharma.
verses.purport: Arjuna declares his unshakeable theological realization: Sri Krishna is the supreme knowable Absolute (Aksharam Paramam), the cosmic foundation (Param Nidhanam), and the protector of Sanatana Dharma.

verses.speaker: अर्जुन उवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
अनादिमध्यान्तमनन्तवीर्य-
मनन्तबाहुं शशिसूर्यनेत्रम् |
पश्यामि त्वां दीप्तहुताशवक्त्रं
स्वतेजसा विश्वमिदं तपन्तम् || १९ ||
verses.sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
अनादिमध्यान्तमनन्तवीर्य-
मनन्तबाहुं शशिसूर्यनेत्रम् |
पश्यामि त्वां दीप्तहुताशवक्त्रं
स्वतेजसा विश्वमिदं तपन्तम् || १९ ||
verses.transliteration:
arjuna uvāca |
anādimadhyāntamanantavīrya-
manantabāhuṃ śaśisūryanetram |
paśyāmi tvāṃ dīptahutāśavaktraṃ
svatejasā viśvamidaṃ tapantam || 19 ||
verses.word_meanings: anādi-madhya-antam—without beginning, middle, or end; ananta-vīryam—of infinite power; ananta-bāhum—with boundless arms; śaśi-sūrya-netram—with the sun and moon as Your eyes; paśyāmi—I see; tvām—You; dīpta-hutāśa-vaktram—with mouths like blazing sacrificial fires; sva-tejasā—by Your own radiance; viśvam idam—this entire universe; tapantam—scorching/illuminating.
verses.translation: I see You without beginning, middle, or end, of boundless prowess, with infinite arms, the sun and moon as Your eyes, mouths blazing like sacrificial fire, scorching and warming this entire universe by Your own radiance!
verses.meaning: The cosmic scale unfolds: The sun and moon are but the eyes of the Cosmic Person; His mouths consume worlds like sacrificial flame, and His fiery energy energizes the cosmos.
verses.purport: The cosmic scale unfolds: The sun and moon are but the eyes of the Cosmic Person; His mouths consume worlds like sacrificial flame, and His fiery energy energizes the cosmos.

verses.speaker: अर्जुन उवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
द्यावापृथिव्योरिदमन्तरं हि
व्याप्तं त्वयैकेन दिशश्च सर्वाः |
दृष्ट्वाद्भुतं रूपमुग्रं तवेदं
लोकत्रयं प्रव्यथितं महात्मन् || २० ||
verses.sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
द्यावापृथिव्योरिदमन्तरं हि
व्याप्तं त्वयैकेन दिशश्च सर्वाः |
दृष्ट्वाद्भुतं रूपमुग्रं तवेदं
लोकत्रयं प्रव्यथितं महात्मन् || २० ||
verses.transliteration:
arjuna uvāca |
dyāvāpṛthivyoridamantaraṃ hi
vyāptaṃ tvayaikena diśaśca sarvāḥ |
dṛṣṭvādbhutaṃ rūpamugraṃ tavedaṃ
lokatrayaṃ pravyathitaṃ mahātman || 20 ||
verses.word_meanings: dyau-ā-pṛthivyoḥ—between heaven and earth; idam antaram—this intermediate space; hi—indeed; vyāptam—is pervaded; tvayā ekena—by You alone; diśaḥ ca sarvāḥ—and all directions; dṛṣṭvā—beholding; adbhutam—wondrous; rūpam—form; ugram—terrible/fierce; tava idam—this of Yours; loka-trayam—the three worlds; pravyathitam—tremble in fear; mahātman—O Great Soul.
verses.translation: The entire space between heaven and earth and all the quarters of the sky are pervaded by You alone! Beholding this wondrous, terrible and awe-inspiring form of Yours, O Great Soul, the three worlds tremble in fear!
verses.meaning: The vision shifts from sublime wonder to overpowering awe. The immense terrifying majesty (Ugra Rupa) fills all spatial dimensions, causing the inhabitants of the three worlds to tremble.
verses.purport: The vision shifts from sublime wonder to overpowering awe. The immense terrifying majesty (Ugra Rupa) fills all spatial dimensions, causing the inhabitants of the three worlds to tremble.

verses.speaker: अर्जुन उवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
अमी हि त्वां सुरसङ्घा विशन्ति
केचिद्भीताः प्राञ्जलयो गृणन्ति |
स्वस्तीत्युक्त्वा महर्षिसिद्धसङ्घाः
स्तुवन्ति त्वां स्तुतिभिः पुष्कलाभिः || २१ ||
verses.sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
अमी हि त्वां सुरसङ्घा विशन्ति
केचिद्भीताः प्राञ्जलयो गृणन्ति |
स्वस्तीत्युक्त्वा महर्षिसिद्धसङ्घाः
स्तुवन्ति त्वां स्तुतिभिः पुष्कलाभिः || २१ ||
verses.transliteration:
arjuna uvāca |
amī hi tvāṃ surasaṅghā viśanti
kecidbhītāḥ prāñjalayo gṛṇanti |
svastītyuktvā maharṣisiddhasaṅghāḥ
stuvanti tvāṃ stutibhiḥ puṣkalābhiḥ || 21 ||
verses.word_meanings: amī—these; hi—indeed; tvām—into You; sura-saṅghāḥ—hosts of celestial gods; viśanti—are entering; kecit—some; bhītāḥ—in awe/fear; prāñjalayaḥ—with folded hands; gṛṇanti—are chanting prayers; svasti iti uktvā—saying 'May peace prevail!'; mahā-ṛṣi-siddha-saṅghāḥ—multitudes of great sages and perfected beings; stuvanti—praise; tvām—You; stutibhiḥ puṣkalābhiḥ—with sublime hymns.
verses.translation: Hosts of celestial gods enter into You; some in awe praise You with folded hands. Multitudes of great sages and perfected beings chant 'May peace prevail!' and glorify You with magnificent hymns.
verses.meaning: Cosmic beings witness the universal revelation: Demigods surrender into the Lord, while enlightened sages offer sublime Vedic mantras of peace (Svasti) before the majestic display of cosmic power.
verses.purport: Cosmic beings witness the universal revelation: Demigods surrender into the Lord, while enlightened sages offer sublime Vedic mantras of peace (Svasti) before the majestic display of cosmic power.

verses.speaker: अर्जुन उवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
रुद्रादित्या वसवो ये च साध्या
विश्वेऽश्विनौ मरुतश्चोष्मपाश्च |
गन्धर्वयक्षासुरसिद्धसङ्घा
वीक्षन्ते त्वां विस्मिताश्चैव सर्वे || २२ ||
verses.sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
रुद्रादित्या वसवो ये च साध्या
विश्वेऽश्विनौ मरुतश्चोष्मपाश्च |
गन्धर्वयक्षासुरसिद्धसङ्घा
वीक्षन्ते त्वां विस्मिताश्चैव सर्वे || २२ ||
verses.transliteration:
arjuna uvāca |
rudrādityā vasavo ye ca sādhyā
viśve'śvinau marutaścoṣmapāśca |
gandharvayakṣāsurasiddhasaṅghā
vīkṣante tvāṃ vismitāścaiva sarve || 22 ||
verses.word_meanings: rudra-ādityāḥ—the Rudras and Adityas; vasavaḥ—the Vasus; ye ca sādhyāḥ—and the Sadhyas; viśve—the Vishvedevas; aśvinau—the twin Ashvins; marutaḥ ca—and the Maruts; ūṣmapāḥ ca—and the ancestral spirits; gandharva-yakṣa-asura-siddha-saṅghāḥ—hosts of Gandharvas, Yakshas, Asuras, and Siddhas; vīkṣante—behold; tvām—You; vismitāḥ—astonished; ca eva sarve—all indeed.
verses.translation: The Rudras, Adityas, Vasus, Sadhyas, Vishvedevas, the twin Ashvins, the Maruts, the Ushmapas (ancestors), and the hosts of Gandharvas, Yakshas, Asuras, and Siddhas—all gaze upon You in total wonder!
verses.meaning: Every echelon of cosmic existence—terrestrial, subterranean, ancestral, and celestial—stands spellbound in reverence before the all-encompassing Vishvarupa.
verses.purport: Every echelon of cosmic existence—terrestrial, subterranean, ancestral, and celestial—stands spellbound in reverence before the all-encompassing Vishvarupa.

verses.speaker: अर्जुन उवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
रूपं महत्ते बहुवक्त्रनेत्रं
महाबाहो बहुबाहूरुपादम् |
बहूदरं बहुदंष्ट्राकरालं
दृष्ट्वा लोकाः प्रव्यथितास्तथाहम् || २३ ||
verses.sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
रूपं महत्ते बहुवक्त्रनेत्रं
महाबाहो बहुबाहूरुपादम् |
बहूदरं बहुदंष्ट्राकरालं
दृष्ट्वा लोकाः प्रव्यथितास्तथाहम् || २३ ||
verses.transliteration:
arjuna uvāca |
rūpaṃ mahatte bahuvaktranetraṃ
mahābāho bahubāhūrupādam |
bahūdaraṃ bahudaṃṣṭrākarālaṃ
dṛṣṭvā lokāḥ pravyathitāstathāham || 23 ||
verses.word_meanings: rūpam mahat—mighty form; te—Your; bahu-vaktra-netram—with countless mouths and eyes; mahā-bāho—O mighty-armed one; bahu-bāhu-ūru-pādam—with countless arms, thighs, and feet; bahu-udaram—with countless bellies; bahu-daṃṣṭrā-karālam—terrible with many fearsome tusks; dṛṣṭvā—beholding; lokāḥ—the worlds; pravyathitāḥ—are terrified; tathā aham—and so am I.
verses.translation: Beholding Your colossal form with its countless mouths and eyes, O mighty-armed Lord, with countless arms, thighs, feet, bellies, and terrifying tusks—all the worlds are struck with terror, and so am I!
verses.meaning: Arjuna confesses his human dread: The Universal Form is not a static pastoral portrait, but an overwhelming, all-consuming cosmic reality bristling with terrible teeth and infinite limbs.
verses.purport: Arjuna confesses his human dread: The Universal Form is not a static pastoral portrait, but an overwhelming, all-consuming cosmic reality bristling with terrible teeth and infinite limbs.

verses.speaker: अर्जुन उवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
नभःस्पृशं दीप्तमनेकवर्णं
व्यात्ताननं दीप्तविशालनेत्रम् |
दृष्ट्वा हि त्वां प्रव्यथितान्तरात्मा
धृतिं न विन्दामि शमं च विष्णो || २४ ||
verses.sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
नभःस्पृशं दीप्तमनेकवर्णं
व्यात्ताननं दीप्तविशालनेत्रम् |
दृष्ट्वा हि त्वां प्रव्यथितान्तरात्मा
धृतिं न विन्दामि शमं च विष्णो || २४ ||
verses.transliteration:
arjuna uvāca |
nabhaḥspṛśaṃ dīptamanekavarṇaṃ
vyāttānanaṃ dīptaviśālanetram |
dṛṣṭvā hi tvāṃ pravyathitāntarātmā
dhṛtiṃ na vindāmi śamaṃ ca viṣṇo || 24 ||
verses.word_meanings: nabhaḥ-spṛśam—touching the sky; dīptam—blazing; aneka-varṇam—multicolored; vyātta-ānanam—with mouths wide open; dīpta-viśāla-netram—with blazing, massive eyes; dṛṣṭvā—beholding; hi—indeed; tvām—You; pravyathita-antarātmā—with my innermost soul trembling; dhṛtim—fortitude/courage; na vindāmi—I find not; śamam ca—nor peace; viṣṇo—O All-Pervading Vishnu.
verses.translation: Touching the skies, effulgent in many colors, with mouths wide open and massive blazing eyes—beholding You, O Vishnu, my innermost soul trembles, and I find neither courage nor peace!
verses.meaning: Arjuna, the bravest warrior on earth who never flinched before any army, feels his inner composure shattered. Addressing Krishna as Vishnu, he begs for relief from the terrifying majesty.
verses.purport: Arjuna, the bravest warrior on earth who never flinched before any army, feels his inner composure shattered. Addressing Krishna as Vishnu, he begs for relief from the terrifying majesty.

verses.speaker: अर्जुन उवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
दंष्ट्राकरालानि च ते मुखानि
दृष्ट्वैव कालानलसन्निभानि |
दिशो न जाने न लभे च शर्म
प्रसीद देवेश जगन्निवास || २५ ||
verses.sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
दंष्ट्राकरालानि च ते मुखानि
दृष्ट्वैव कालानलसन्निभानि |
दिशो न जाने न लभे च शर्म
प्रसीद देवेश जगन्निवास || २५ ||
verses.transliteration:
arjuna uvāca |
daṃṣṭrākarālāni ca te mukhāni
dṛṣṭvaiva kālānalasannibhāni |
diśo na jāne na labhe ca śarma
prasīda deveśa jagannivāsa || 25 ||
verses.word_meanings: daṃṣṭrā-karālāni—fearsome with tusks; ca—and; te—Your; mukhāni—mouths/faces; dṛṣṭvā eva—having seen; kāla-anala-sannibhāni—resembling the blazing fires of cosmic dissolution (Kalanala); diśaḥ—directions; na jāne—I know not; na labhe—I find not; ca—and; śarma—peace/solace; prasīda—have mercy/be gracious; deva-īśa—O Lord of gods; jagat-nivāsa—O Abode of the Universe.
verses.translation: Seeing Your mouths fearsome with tusks, blazing like the fires of cosmic dissolution, I lose all sense of direction and find no peace. Be gracious, O Lord of gods, O Abode of the Universe!
verses.meaning: The terrifying destructive aspect of Time (Kalanala) disorients Arjuna. He cries out: 'Prasīda Deveśa Jagannivāsa!'—beseeching divine grace and mercy.
verses.purport: The terrifying destructive aspect of Time (Kalanala) disorients Arjuna. He cries out: 'Prasīda Deveśa Jagannivāsa!'—beseeching divine grace and mercy.

verses.speaker: अर्जुन उवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
अमी च त्वां धृतराष्ट्रस्य पुत्राः
सर्वे सहैवावनिपालसङ्घैः |
भीष्मो द्रोणः सूतपुत्रस्तथासौ
सहास्मदीयैरपि योधमुख्यैः || २६ ||
verses.sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
अमी च त्वां धृतराष्ट्रस्य पुत्राः
सर्वे सहैवावनिपालसङ्घैः |
भीष्मो द्रोणः सूतपुत्रस्तथासौ
सहास्मदीयैरपि योधमुख्यैः || २६ ||
verses.transliteration:
arjuna uvāca |
amī ca tvāṃ dhṛtarāṣṭrasya putrāḥ
sarve sahaivāvanipālasaṅghaiḥ |
bhīṣmo droṇaḥ sūtaputrastathāsau
sahāsmadīyairapi yodhamukhyaiḥ || 26 ||
verses.word_meanings: amī ca—and all these; tvām—into You; dhṛtarāṣṭrasya putrāḥ—the sons of Dhritarashtra (Kauravas); sarve—all; saha eva—along with; avanipāla-saṅghaiḥ—hosts of allied kings; bhīṣmaḥ—Bhishma; droṇaḥ—Drona; sūta-putraḥ tathā asau—and Karna (the charioteer's son); saha—together with; asmadīyaiḥ api—our own also; yodha-mukhyaiḥ—chief warrior generals.
verses.translation: And all these sons of Dhritarashtra with their allied kings, Bhishma, Drona, and that Karna, along with the principal warriors of our own army as well—
verses.meaning: Arjuna witnesses the preordained destiny of the Kurukshetra war: Both rival armies, including revered elders Bhishma and Drona, heroic Karna, and the Pandava generals, are already being drawn into the jaws of cosmic destiny.
verses.purport: Arjuna witnesses the preordained destiny of the Kurukshetra war: Both rival armies, including revered elders Bhishma and Drona, heroic Karna, and the Pandava generals, are already being drawn into the jaws of cosmic destiny.

verses.speaker: अर्जुन उवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
वक्त्राणि ते त्वरमाणा विशन्ति
दंष्ट्राकरालानि भयानकानि |
केचिद्विलग्ना दशनान्तरेषु
संदृश्यन्ते चूर्णितैरुत्तमाङ्गैः || २७ ||
verses.sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
वक्त्राणि ते त्वरमाणा विशन्ति
दंष्ट्राकरालानि भयानकानि |
केचिद्विलग्ना दशनान्तरेषु
संदृश्यन्ते चूर्णितैरुत्तमाङ्गैः || २७ ||
verses.transliteration:
arjuna uvāca |
vaktrāṇi te tvaramāṇā viśanti
daṃṣṭrākarālāni bhayānakāni |
kecidvilagnā daśanāntareṣu
saṃdṛśyante cūrṇitairuttamāṅgaiḥ || 27 ||
verses.word_meanings: vaktrāṇi te—into Your mouths; tvaramāṇāḥ—rushing headlong; viśanti—they enter; daṃṣṭrā-karālāni—fearsome with tusks; bhayānakāni—terrible; kecit—some; vilagnāḥ—caught/crushed; daśana-antareṣu—between Your teeth; saṃdṛśyante—are seen; cūrṇitaiḥ uttama-aṅgaiḥ—with crushed heads.
verses.translation: Are rushing headlong into Your fearsome, terrifying mouths! Some are seen caught between Your teeth with their heads crushed to powder!
verses.meaning: The graphic vision of inexorable mortality: No earthly power or military armor can withstand the crushing march of Time. All warriors are rushing helplessly into the fiery jaws of dissolution.
verses.purport: The graphic vision of inexorable mortality: No earthly power or military armor can withstand the crushing march of Time. All warriors are rushing helplessly into the fiery jaws of dissolution.

verses.speaker: अर्जुन उवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
यथा नदीनां बहवोऽम्बुवेगाः
समुद्रमेवाभिमुखा द्रवन्ति |
तथा तवामी नरलोकवीरा
विशन्ति वक्त्राण्यभिविज्वलन्ति || २८ ||
verses.sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
यथा नदीनां बहवोऽम्बुवेगाः
समुद्रमेवाभिमुखा द्रवन्ति |
तथा तवामी नरलोकवीरा
विशन्ति वक्त्राण्यभिविज्वलन्ति || २८ ||
verses.transliteration:
arjuna uvāca |
yathā nadīnāṃ bahavo'mbuvegāḥ
samudramevābhimukhā dravanti |
tathā tavāmī naralokavīrā
viśanti vaktrāṇyabhivijvalanti || 28 ||
verses.word_meanings: yathā—as; nadīnām—of rivers; bahavaḥ ambu-vegāḥ—many rapid torrents of water; samudram eva—into the ocean indeed; abhimukhāḥ—heading towards; dravanti—flow/rush; tathā—similarly; tava—Your; amī—these; nara-loka-vīrāḥ—heroes of the mortal world; viśanti—enter; vaktrāṇi—into mouths; abhivijvalanti—blazing on all sides.
verses.translation: As the many rapid torrents of rivers rush headlong into the ocean, so do these heroes of the mortal world enter into Your blazing mouths!
verses.meaning: A sublime poetic metaphor: Just as rivers cannot halt their flow toward the sea, mortal souls and proud armies cannot escape their ultimate destination in the ocean of Cosmic Time.
verses.purport: A sublime poetic metaphor: Just as rivers cannot halt their flow toward the sea, mortal souls and proud armies cannot escape their ultimate destination in the ocean of Cosmic Time.

verses.speaker: अर्जुन उवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
यथा प्रदीप्तं ज्वलनं पतङ्गा
विशन्ति नाशाय समृद्धवेगाः |
तथैव नाशाय विशन्ति लोका-
स्तवापि वक्त्राणि समृद्धवेगाः || २९ ||
verses.sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
यथा प्रदीप्तं ज्वलनं पतङ्गा
विशन्ति नाशाय समृद्धवेगाः |
तथैव नाशाय विशन्ति लोका-
स्तवापि वक्त्राणि समृद्धवेगाः || २९ ||
verses.transliteration:
arjuna uvāca |
yathā pradīptaṃ jvalanaṃ pataṅgā
viśanti nāśāya samṛddhavegāḥ |
tathaiva nāśāya viśanti lokā-
stavāpi vaktrāṇi samṛddhavegāḥ || 29 ||
verses.word_meanings: yathā—as; pradīptam—blazing; jvalanam—fire; pataṅgāḥ—moths; viśanti—enter; nāśāya—unto destruction; samṛddha-vegāḥ—with gathering speed; tathā eva—similarly; nāśāya—unto destruction; viśanti—enter; lokāḥ—all beings/people; tava api—Your also; vaktrāṇi—mouths; samṛddha-vegāḥ—with rushing speed.
verses.translation: As moths rush with gathering speed into a blazing fire unto their destruction, so do all these worlds rush with intense speed into Your mouths unto their doom!
verses.meaning: Second poignant metaphor: Blinded by pride, greed, and delusion, human beings rush into the flames of conflict and death just like moths into a nocturnal flame.
verses.purport: Second poignant metaphor: Blinded by pride, greed, and delusion, human beings rush into the flames of conflict and death just like moths into a nocturnal flame.

verses.speaker: अर्जुन उवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
लेलिह्यसे ग्रसमानः समन्ता-
ल्लोकान्समग्रान्वदनैर्ज्वलद्भिः |
तेजोभिरापूर्य जगत्समग्रं
भासस्तवोग्राः प्रतपन्ति विष्णो || ३० ||
verses.sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
लेलिह्यसे ग्रसमानः समन्ता-
ल्लोकान्समग्रान्वदनैर्ज्वलद्भिः |
तेजोभिरापूर्य जगत्समग्रं
भासस्तवोग्राः प्रतपन्ति विष्णो || ३० ||
verses.transliteration:
arjuna uvāca |
lelihyase grasamānaḥ samantā-
llokānsamagrānvadanairjvaladbhiḥ |
tejobhirāpūrya jagatsamagraṃ
bhāsastavogrāḥ pratapanti viṣṇo || 30 ||
verses.word_meanings: lelihyase—You lick Your lips; grasamānaḥ—devouring; samantāt—from all sides; lokān samagrān—all the worlds; vadanaiḥ jvaladbhiḥ—with blazing mouths; tejobhiḥ—with fierce radiant energy; āpūrya—filling; jagat samagram—the entire universe; bhāsaḥ—rays/splendors; tava ugrāḥ—Your terrible; pratapanti—scorch; viṣṇo—O Vishnu.
verses.translation: You lick Your lips as You devour all the worlds from every side with Your blazing mouths! Filling the entire universe with fiery brilliance, Your terrible radiance is scorching the cosmos, O Vishnu!
verses.meaning: The all-devouring hunger of cosmic dissolution: The Lord's radiant rays fill every corner of existence, purifying and consuming the universe at the end of a cycle.
verses.purport: The all-devouring hunger of cosmic dissolution: The Lord's radiant rays fill every corner of existence, purifying and consuming the universe at the end of a cycle.

verses.speaker: अर्जुन उवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
आख्याहि मे को भवानुग्ररूपो
नमोऽस्तु ते देववर प्रसीद |
विज्ञाpermissionतुमिच्छामि भवन्तमाद्यं
न हि प्रजानामि तव प्रवृत्तिम् || ३१ ||
verses.sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
आख्याहि मे को भवानुग्ररूपो
नमोऽस्तु ते देववर प्रसीद |
विज्ञातुमिच्छामि भवन्तमाद्यं
न हि प्रजानामि तव प्रवृत्तिम् || ३१ ||
verses.transliteration:
arjuna uvāca |
ākhyāhi me ko bhavānugrarūpo
namo'stu te devavara prasīda |
vijñātumicchāmi bhavantamādyaṃ
na hi prajānāmi tava pravṛttim || 31 ||
verses.word_meanings: ākhyāhi me—tell me; kaḥ bhavān—who You are; ugra-rūpaḥ—of terrifying form; namaḥ astu te—salutations unto You; deva-vara—O supreme God; prasīda—be gracious; vijñātum icchāmi—I desire to know; bhavantam—You; ādyam—the Primeval One; na hi prajānāmi—for I do not understand; tava pravṛttim—Your mission/working.
verses.translation: Tell me, who are You of such terrifying form? Salutations unto You, O Supreme God! Have mercy! I desire to know You, the Primeval One, for I do not comprehend Your cosmic working!
verses.meaning: Arjuna asks the climactic question: 'Ākhyāhi me ko bhavān ugra-rūpaḥ?' (Tell me, who are You in this terrifying form?). He yearns to understand the divine purpose behind this cosmic destruction.
verses.purport: Arjuna asks the climactic question: 'Ākhyāhi me ko bhavān ugra-rūpaḥ?' (Tell me, who are You in this terrifying form?). He yearns to understand the divine purpose behind this cosmic destruction.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
कालोऽस्मि लोकक्षयकृत्प्रवृद्धो
लोकान्समाहर्तुमिह प्रवृत्ततः |
ऋतेऽपि त्वां न भविष्यन्ति सर्वे
येऽवस्थिताः प्रत्यनीकेषु योधाः || ३२ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
कालोऽस्मि लोकक्षयकृत्प्रवृद्धो
लोकान्समाहर्तुमिह प्रवृत्तः |
ऋतेऽपि त्वां न भविष्यन्ति सर्वे
येऽवस्थिताः प्रत्यनीकेषु योधाः || ३२ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
kālo'smi lokakṣayakṛtpravṛddho
lokānsamāhartumiha pravṛttaḥ |
ṛte'pi tvāṃ na bhaviṣyanti sarve
ye'vasthitāḥ pratyanīkeṣu yodhāḥ || 32 ||
verses.word_meanings: śrī-bhagavān uvāca—the Supreme Lord said; kālaḥ asmi—I am Time/Death; loka-kṣaya-kṛt—the destroyer of the worlds; pravṛddhaḥ—mighty/grown mature; lokān—the worlds; samāhartum—to destroy/reclaim; iha—here; pravṛttaḥ—engaged/manifested; ṛte api tvām—even without you; na bhaviṣyanti—shall not survive; sarve—all; ye avasthitāḥ—who are stationed; pratyanīkeṣu—in opposing armies; yodhāḥ—the warriors.
verses.translation: The Supreme Lord said: I am Time (Kala), the great destroyer of worlds, manifested here to annihilate all people. Even without your participation, none of the warriors stationed in the opposing armies shall survive!
verses.meaning: One of the supreme utterances of the Bhagavad Gita: Sri Krishna reveals His identity as inexorable Time (Kala). The karmic destiny of the unrighteous warriors has already culminated; their demise is decreed by cosmic law whether Arjuna fights or not.
verses.purport: One of the supreme utterances of the Bhagavad Gita: Sri Krishna reveals His identity as inexorable Time (Kala). The karmic destiny of the unrighteous warriors has already culminated; their demise is decreed by cosmic law whether Arjuna fights or not.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
तस्मात्त्वमुत्तिष्ठ यशो लभस्व
जित्वा शत्रून्भुङ्क्ष्व राज्यं समृद्धम् |
मयैवैते निहताः पूर्वमेव
निमित्तमात्रं भव सव्यसाचिन् || ३३ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
तस्मात्त्वमुत्तिष्ठ यशो लभस्व
जित्वा शत्रून्भुङ्क्ष्व राज्यं समृद्धम् |
मयैवैते निहताः पूर्वमेव
निमित्तमात्रं भव सव्यसाचिन् || ३३ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
tasmāttvamuttiṣṭha yaśo labhasva
jitvā śatrūnbhuṅkṣva rājyaṃ samṛddham |
mayaivaite nihatāḥ pūrvameva
nimittamātraṃ bhava savyasācin || 33 ||
verses.word_meanings: tasmāt—therefore; tvam uttiṣṭha—arise you; yaśaḥ labhasva—attain glory; jitvā śatrūn—conquering enemies; bhuṅkṣva—enjoy; rājyam samṛddham—a prosperous kingdom; mayā eva—by Me alone; ete—all these; nihatāḥ—are already slain; pūrvam eva—already in advance; nimitta-mātram—merely an instrument; bhava—become; savya-sācin—O ambidextrous archer (Arjuna).
verses.translation: Therefore arise, win glory, conquer your foes, and enjoy a prosperous kingdom! By Me alone have these warriors already been slain in advance; be merely an instrument (Nimitta-matram), O ambidextrous archer (Savyasachin)!
verses.meaning: The ultimate call to dharmic action: The cosmic outcome has already been settled by Divine Will ('Mayaivaite nihatāḥ pūrvam eva'). Arjuna is invited not to create the victory, but to participate honorably as a pure instrument ('Nimitta-mātram') of divine righteousness.
verses.purport: The ultimate call to dharmic action: The cosmic outcome has already been settled by Divine Will ('Mayaivaite nihatāḥ pūrvam eva'). Arjuna is invited not to create the victory, but to participate honorably as a pure instrument ('Nimitta-mātram') of divine righteousness.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
द्रोणं च भीष्मं च जयद्रथं च
कर्णं तथान्यानपि योधवीरान् |
मया हतांस्त्वं जहि मा व्यथिष्ठा
युध्यस्व जेतासि रणे सपत्नान् || ३४ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
द्रोणं च भीष्मं च जयद्रथं च
कर्णं तथान्यानपि योधवीरान् |
मया हतांस्त्वं जहि मा व्यथिष्ठा
युध्यस्व जेतासि रणे सपत्नान् || ३४ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
droṇaṃ ca bhīṣmaṃ ca jayadrathaṃ ca
karṇaṃ tathānyānapi yodhavīrān |
mayā hatāṃstvaṃ jahi mā vyathiṣṭhā
yudhyasva jetāsi raṇe sapatnān || 34 ||
verses.word_meanings: droṇam ca—Drona also; bhīṣmam ca—and Bhishma; jayadratham ca—and Jayadratha; karṇam—Karna; tathā—also; anyān api—other also; yodha-vīrān—heroic warriors; mayā hatān—slain by Me; tvam jahi—you slay; mā vyathiṣṭhāḥ—do not be distressed/grieve; yudhyasva—fight; jetā asi—you shall conquer; raṇe—in battle; sapatnān—your adversaries.
verses.translation: Drona, Bhishma, Jayadratha, Karna, and all the other heroic warriors have already been slain by Me! Slay them without hesitation, do not grieve; fight, and you shall conquer your adversaries in battle!
verses.meaning: Sri Krishna dissolves Arjuna's emotional hesitation regarding his teachers and kin: Because their karmic debt has matured, the Lord has already withdrawn their lifespan. Arjuna's duty is to discharge his warrior code without personal hatred or guilt.
verses.purport: Sri Krishna dissolves Arjuna's emotional hesitation regarding his teachers and kin: Because their karmic debt has matured, the Lord has already withdrawn their lifespan. Arjuna's duty is to discharge his warrior code without personal hatred or guilt.

verses.speaker: सञ्जय उवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
सञ्जय उवाच |
एतच्छ्रुत्वा वचनं केशवस्य
कृताञ्जलिर्वेपमानः किरीटी |
नमस्कृत्वा भूय एवाह कृष्णं
सगद्गदं भीतभीतः प्रणम्य || ३५ ||
verses.sanskrit:
सञ्जय उवाच |
एतच्छ्रुत्वा वचनं केशवस्य
कृताञ्जलिर्वेपमानः किरीटी |
नमस्कृत्वा भूय एवाह कृष्णं
सगद्गदं भीतभीतः प्रणम्य || ३५ ||
verses.transliteration:
sañjaya uvāca |
etacchrutvā vacanaṃ keśavasya
kṛtāñjalirvepamānaḥ kirīṭī |
namaskṛtvā bhūya evāha kṛṣṇaṃ
sagadgadaṃ bhītabhītaḥ praṇamya || 35 ||
verses.word_meanings: sañjayaḥ uvāca—Sanjaya said; etat śrutvā—hearing these; vacanam—words; keśavasya—of Keshava; kṛta-añjaliḥ—with folded hands; vepamānaḥ—trembling; kirīṭī—the crowned one (Arjuna); namaskṛtvā—offering obeisances; bhūyaḥ eva—again further; āha—spoke; kṛṣṇam—unto Krishna; sa-gadgadam—with a faltering voice; bhīta-bhītaḥ—overwhelmed with awe and fear; praṇamya—bowing down.
verses.translation: Sanjaya said: Hearing these words of Keshava, the crowned Arjuna, trembling and with folded hands, bowed down again and again, and with a faltering voice choked with awe, addressed Krishna:
verses.meaning: Sanjaya depicts Arjuna's complete transformation: Struck to the depths of his soul by the realization of Krishna's cosmic supremacy, Arjuna speaks with a voice trembling with sacred emotion.
verses.purport: Sanjaya depicts Arjuna's complete transformation: Struck to the depths of his soul by the realization of Krishna's cosmic supremacy, Arjuna speaks with a voice trembling with sacred emotion.

verses.speaker: अर्जुन उवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
स्थाने हृषीकेश तव प्रकीर्त्या
जगत्प्रहृष्यत्यनुरज्यते च |
रक्षांसि भीतानि दिशो द्रवन्ति
सर्वे नमस्यन्ति च सिद्धसङ्घाः || ३६ ||
verses.sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
स्थाने हृषीकेश तव प्रकीर्त्या
जगत्प्रहृष्यत्यनुरज्यते च |
रक्षांसि भीतानि दिशो द्रवन्ति
सर्वे नमस्यन्ति च सिद्धसङ्घाः || ३६ ||
verses.transliteration:
arjuna uvāca |
sthāne hṛṣīkeśa tava prakīrtyā
jagatprahṛṣyatyanurajyate ca |
rakṣāṃsi bhītāni diśo dravanti
sarve namasyanti ca siddhasaṅghāḥ || 36 ||
verses.word_meanings: arjunaḥ uvāca—Arjuna said; sthāne—rightly/fittingly; hṛṣīkeśa—O Hrishikesha (Lord of the senses); tava prakīrtyā—by singing Your glories; jagat—the universe; prahṛṣyati—rejoices; anurajyate ca—and becomes attached in love; rakṣāṃsi—demons; bhītāni—frightened; diśaḥ—in all directions; dravanti—flee; sarve—all; namasyanti ca—and bow in reverence; siddha-saṅghāḥ—the hosts of perfected beings.
verses.translation: Arjuna said: Rightly, O Hrishikesha, does the entire universe rejoice and delight in singing Your glories! The demons flee in terror in all directions, while all the hosts of perfected saints bow down in adoration!
verses.meaning: Arjuna begins his celebrated hymn of universal praise: It is entirely right and cosmic order (Sthane) that virtuous souls rejoice in Krishna's name while dark, egoic forces flee before His divine light.
verses.purport: Arjuna begins his celebrated hymn of universal praise: It is entirely right and cosmic order (Sthane) that virtuous souls rejoice in Krishna's name while dark, egoic forces flee before His divine light.

verses.speaker: अर्जुन उवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
कस्माच्च ते न नमेरन्महात्मन्
गरीयसे ब्रह्मणोऽप्यादिकर्त्रे |
अनन्त देवेश जगन्निवास
त्वमक्षरं सदसत्तत्परं यत् || ३७ ||
verses.sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
कस्माच्च ते न नमेरन्महात्मन्
गरीयसे ब्रह्मणोऽप्यादिकर्त्रे |
अनन्त देवेश जगन्निवास
त्वमक्षरं सदसत्तत्परं यत् || ३७ ||
verses.transliteration:
arjuna uvāca |
kasmācca te na nameranmahātman
garīyase brahmaṇo'pyādikartre |
ananta deveśa jagannivāsa
tvamakṣaraṃ sadasattatparaṃ yat || 37 ||
verses.word_meanings: kasmāt ca—and why; te—unto You; na nameran—should they not bow; mahātman—O Great Soul; garīyase—who are greater; brahmaṇaḥ api—even than Brahma; ādi-kartre—the Original Creator; ananta—O Infinite One; deva-īśa—O Lord of gods; jagat-nivāsa—O Refuge of the universe; tvam—You are; akṣaram—the Imperishable; sat-asat—being and non-being; tat-param yat—that which is beyond both.
verses.translation: And why should they not bow to You, O Great Soul, who are greater even than Brahma, the Original Creator? O Infinite One, God of gods, Refuge of the universe, You are the Imperishable (Akshara), Being (Sat), Non-being (Asat), and that which transcends both!
verses.meaning: Arjuna exalts Krishna above Brahma: Krishna is the original source even of the creator Brahma. He is Akshara (the indestructible), Sat (manifest existence), Asat (unmanifest potential), and Param (transcendent Absolute).
verses.purport: Arjuna exalts Krishna above Brahma: Krishna is the original source even of the creator Brahma. He is Akshara (the indestructible), Sat (manifest existence), Asat (unmanifest potential), and Param (transcendent Absolute).

verses.speaker: अर्जुन उवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
त्वमादिदेवः पुरुषः पुराण-
स्त्वमस्य विश्वस्य परं निधानम् |
वेत्तासि वेद्यं च परं च धाम
त्वया ततं विश्वमनन्तरूप || ३८ ||
verses.sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
त्वमादिदेवः पुरुषः पुराण-
स्त्वमस्य विश्वस्य परं निधानम् |
वेत्तासि वेद्यं च परं च धाम
त्वया ततं विश्वमनन्तरूप || ३८ ||
verses.transliteration:
arjuna uvāca |
tvamādidevaḥ puruṣaḥ purāṇa-
stvamasya viśvasya paraṃ nidhānam |
vettāsi vedyaṃ ca paraṃ ca dhāma
tvayā tataṃ viśvamanantarūpa || 38 ||
verses.word_meanings: tvam—You are; ādi-devaḥ—the Primeval Deity; puruṣaḥ purāṇaḥ—the Ancient Person; tvam—You are; asya viśvasya—of this universe; param nidhānam—the supreme refuge/treasure; vettā asi—You are the knower; vedyam ca—and the object to be known; param ca dhāma—and the supreme abode; tvayā—by You; tatam—is pervaded; viśvam—the universe; ananta-rūpa—O One of boundless form.
verses.translation: You are the Primeval Deity, the Ancient Divine Person, the supreme refuge of this entire universe! You are the Knower, the Object of Knowledge, and the Supreme Abode. By You alone is this entire universe pervaded, O One of boundless form!
verses.meaning: A magnificent synthesis of theological truths: Krishna is both the knower (Vetta) and the known (Vedya), the origin (Adi-deva) and the final resting place (Param Dhama).
verses.purport: A magnificent synthesis of theological truths: Krishna is both the knower (Vetta) and the known (Vedya), the origin (Adi-deva) and the final resting place (Param Dhama).

verses.speaker: अर्जुन उवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
वायुर्यमोऽग्निर्वरुणः शशाङ्कः
प्रजापतिस्त्वं प्रपितामहश्च |
नमो नमस्तेऽस्तु सहस्रकृत्वः
पुनश्च भूयोऽपि नमो नमस्ते || ३९ ||
verses.sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
वायुर्यमोऽग्निर्वरुणः शशाङ्कः
प्रजापतिस्त्वं प्रपितामहश्च |
नमो नमस्तेऽस्तु सहस्रकृत्वः
पुनश्च भूयोऽपि नमो नमस्ते || ३९ ||
verses.transliteration:
arjuna uvāca |
vāyuryamo'gnirvaruṇaḥ śaśāṅkaḥ
prajāpatistvaṃ prapitāmahaśca |
namo namaste'stu sahasrakṛtvaḥ
punaśca bhūyo'pi namo namaste || 39 ||
verses.word_meanings: vāyuḥ—the wind; yamaḥ—the lord of death/justice; agniḥ—fire; varuṇaḥ—water deity; śaśāṅkaḥ—the moon; prajāpatiḥ—the progenitor (Brahma); tvam—You are; prapitāmahaḥ ca—and the Great-Grandfather; namaḥ namaste astu—salutations, salutations unto You; sahasra-kṛtvaḥ—a thousand times; punaḥ ca—and again; bhūyaḥ api—and yet again; namaḥ namaste—salutations, salutations unto You.
verses.translation: You are the Wind, the Lord of Justice (Yama), Fire (Agni), the Ocean Lord (Varuna), the Moon (Shashanka), the Progenitor (Prajapati), and the Great-Grandfather of all creation! Salutations, salutations unto You a thousand times, and again and yet again, salutations, salutations unto You!
verses.meaning: Arjuna pours out ecstatic prostrations: 'Namo namaste 'stu sahasra-kṛtvaḥ punaś ca bhūyo 'pi namo namas te' (A thousand salutations to You, and again and again a thousand salutations!).
verses.purport: Arjuna pours out ecstatic prostrations: 'Namo namaste 'stu sahasra-kṛtvaḥ punaś ca bhūyo 'pi namo namas te' (A thousand salutations to You, and again and again a thousand salutations!).

verses.speaker: अर्जुन उवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
नमः पुरस्तादथ पृष्ठतस्ते
नमोऽस्तु ते सर्वत एव सर्व |
अनन्तवीर्यामितविक्रमस्त्वं
सर्वं समाप्नोषि ततोऽसि सर्वः || ४० ||
verses.sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
नमः पुरस्तादथ पृष्ठतस्ते
नमोऽस्तु ते सर्वत एव सर्व |
अनन्तवीर्यामितविक्रमस्त्वं
सर्वं समाप्नोषि ततोऽसि सर्वः || ४० ||
verses.transliteration:
arjuna uvāca |
namaḥ purastādatha pṛṣṭhataste
namo'stu te sarvata eva sarva |
anantavīryāmitavikramastvaṃ
sarvaṃ samāpnoṣi tato'si sarvaḥ || 40 ||
verses.word_meanings: namaḥ purastāt—salutations in front; atha pṛṣṭhataḥ te—and behind You; namaḥ astu te—salutations unto You; sarvataḥ eva—from all sides indeed; sarva—O All-Encompassing One; ananta-vīrya—of infinite strength; amita-vikramaḥ—of boundless might; tvam—You; sarvam—everything; samāpnoṣi—pervade/encompass; tataḥ—therefore; asi sarvaḥ—You are All.
verses.translation: Salutations unto You in front, salutations behind You, salutations to You from every side, O All! Boundless in power and immeasurable in might, You pervade everything, and therefore You are Everything!
verses.meaning: The realization of complete non-dual pantheism and panentheism: Because Sri Krishna fully pervades and sustains all reality, He is not merely an inhabitant of creation—He is the Totality (Sarva) itself.
verses.purport: The realization of complete non-dual pantheism and panentheism: Because Sri Krishna fully pervades and sustains all reality, He is not merely an inhabitant of creation—He is the Totality (Sarva) itself.

verses.speaker: अर्जुन उवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
सखेति मत्वा प्रसभं यदुक्तं
हे कृष्ण हे यादव हे सखेति |
अजानता महिमानं तवेदं
मया प्रमादात्प्रणयेन वापि || ४१ ||
verses.sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
सखेति मत्वा प्रसभं यदुक्तं
हे कृष्ण हे यादव हे सखेति |
अजानता महिमानं तवेदं
मया प्रमादात्प्रणयेन वापि || ४१ ||
verses.transliteration:
arjuna uvāca |
sakheti matvā prasabhaṃ yaduktaṃ
he kṛṣṇa he yādava he sakheti |
ajānatā mahimānaṃ tavedaṃ
mayā pramādātpraṇayena vāpi || 41 ||
verses.word_meanings: sakhā iti matvā—considering You a companion/friend; prasabham—rashly/presumptuously; yat uktam—whatever was said; he kṛṣṇa—O Krishna; he yādava—O Yadava; he sakhā iti—O comrade!; ajānatā—ignorant of; mahimānam—greatness/majesty; tava idam—this of Yours; mayā—by me; pramādāt—out of negligence/carelessness; praṇayena vā api—or out of affection and love.
verses.translation: Thinking of You merely as a friend, whatever rash words I have spoken addressing You as 'O Krishna! O Yadava! O Comrade!', unaware of this majesty of Yours, either out of carelessness or intimate affection—
verses.meaning: Arjuna recalls with humility and remorse how casually he treated Krishna in daily life, joking with Him and calling Him friend, unaware that his companion was the Supreme Lord of all cosmos.
verses.purport: Arjuna recalls with humility and remorse how casually he treated Krishna in daily life, joking with Him and calling Him friend, unaware that his companion was the Supreme Lord of all cosmos.

verses.speaker: अर्जुन उवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
यच्चावहासार्थमसत्कृतोऽसि
विहारशय्यासनभोजनेषु |
एकोऽथवाप्यच्युत तत्समक्षं
तत्क्षामये त्वामहमप्रमेयम् || ४२ ||
verses.sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
यच्चावहासार्थमसत्कृतोऽसि
विहारशय्यासनभोजनेषु |
एकोऽथवाप्यच्युत तत्समक्षं
तत्क्षामये त्वामहमप्रमेयम् || ४२ ||
verses.transliteration:
arjuna uvāca |
yaccāvahāsārthamasatkṛto'si
vihāraśayyāsanabhojaneṣu |
eko'thavāpyacyuta tatsamakṣaṃ
tatkṣāmaye tvāmahamaprameyam || 42 ||
verses.word_meanings: yat ca—and whatever; avahāsa-artham—in jest/amusement; asatkṛtaḥ asi—You were treated disrespectfully/casually; vihāra-śayyā-āsana-bhojaneṣu—while walking, resting, sitting, or dining; ekaḥ—alone; athavā api—or; acyuta—O Infallible One; tat-samakṣam—in the presence of others; tat—for all that; kṣāmaye—I beg forgiveness; tvām—You; aham—I; aprameyam—the Immeasurable One.
verses.translation: And whatever disrespect I may have shown You in jest while resting, sitting, walking, or dining together, whether alone or in the presence of others, O Infallible One—for all that, I beg Your forgiveness, O Immeasurable Lord!
verses.meaning: Arjuna pleads for forgiveness for any casual familiarity. The realization of transcendence casts earthly relations into perspective, making the devotee seek divine grace.
verses.purport: Arjuna pleads for forgiveness for any casual familiarity. The realization of transcendence casts earthly relations into perspective, making the devotee seek divine grace.

verses.speaker: अर्जुन उवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
पितासि लोकस्य चराचरस्य
त्वमस्य पूज्यश्च गुरुर्गरीयान् |
न त्वत्समोऽस्त्यभ्यधिकः कुतोऽन्यो
लोकत्रयेऽप्यप्रतिमप्रभाव || ४३ ||
verses.sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
पितासि लोकस्य चराचरस्य
त्वमस्य पूज्यश्च गुरुर्गरीयान् |
न त्वत्समोऽस्त्यभ्यधिकः कुतोऽन्यो
लोकत्रयेऽप्यप्रतिमप्रभाव || ४३ ||
verses.transliteration:
arjuna uvāca |
pitāsi lokasya carācarasya
tvamasya pūjyaśca gururgarīyān |
na tvatsamo'styabhyadhikaḥ kuto'nyo
lokatraye'pyapratimaprabhāva || 43 ||
verses.word_meanings: pitā asi—You are the Father; lokasya—of the world; cara-acarasya—of the moving and unmoving; tvam—You are; asya—of this; pūjyaḥ ca—worthy of worship; guruḥ garīyān—the supreme Guru of gurus; na tvat-samaḥ asti—there is none equal to You; abhyadhikaḥ kutaḥ anyaḥ—how could there be anyone superior; loka-traye api—in all the three worlds; apratima-prabhāva—O One of peerless majesty.
verses.translation: You are the Father of all this world, moving and unmoving! You are its supreme worshipful Guru, the greatest of the great! There is none equal to You in all the three worlds—how then could anyone surpass You, O Lord of peerless majesty?
verses.meaning: Krishna is hailed as the supreme spiritual master of the universe (Jagadguru) and the procreative father of life, unequaled (Tvatsamo 'sti) and unsurpassable across all dimensions.
verses.purport: Krishna is hailed as the supreme spiritual master of the universe (Jagadguru) and the procreative father of life, unequaled (Tvatsamo 'sti) and unsurpassable across all dimensions.

verses.speaker: अर्जुन उवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
तस्मात्प्रणम्य प्रणिधाय कायं
प्रसादये त्वामहमीशमीड्यम् |
पितेव पुत्रस्य सखेव सख्युः
प्रियः प्रियायार्हसि देव सोढुम् || ४४ ||
verses.sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
तस्मात्प्रणम्य प्रणिधाय कायं
प्रसादये त्वामहमीशमीड्यम् |
पितेव पुत्रस्य सखेव सख्युः
प्रियः प्रियायार्हसि देव सोढुम् || ४४ ||
verses.transliteration:
arjuna uvāca |
tasmātpraṇamya praṇidhāya kāyaṃ
prasādaye tvāmahamīśamīḍyam |
piteva putrasya sakheva sakhyuḥ
priyaḥ priyāyārhasi deva soḍhum || 44 ||
verses.word_meanings: tasmāt—therefore; praṇamya—bowing down; praṇidhāya kāyam—prostrating the body flat on the ground; prasādaye—I seek grace; tvām—You; aham—I; īśam īḍyam—the Adorable Lord; pitā iva putrasya—as a father with his son; sakhā iva sakhyuḥ—as a friend with his friend; priyaḥ priyāyāḥ—as a lover with his beloved; arhasi deva soḍhum—You should forgive/bear with me, O Lord.
verses.translation: Therefore, bowing low and prostrating my whole body before You, I seek Your grace, O Adorable Lord! As a father bears with his son, as a friend with a friend, as a lover with his beloved—so please, O Lord, bear with me and forgive me!
verses.meaning: One of the most touching prayers in world scripture: Arjuna captures the three intimate relationships of divine love—Vatsalya (father-son), Sakhya (friend-friend), and Madhurya (lover-beloved)—asking Krishna to forgive him with tender affection.
verses.purport: One of the most touching prayers in world scripture: Arjuna captures the three intimate relationships of divine love—Vatsalya (father-son), Sakhya (friend-friend), and Madhurya (lover-beloved)—asking Krishna to forgive him with tender affection.

verses.speaker: अर्जुन उवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
अदृष्टपूर्वं हृषितोऽस्मि दृष्ट्वा
भयेन च प्रव्यथितं मनो मे |
तदेव मे दर्शय देव रूपं
प्रसीद देवेश जगन्निवास || ४५ ||
verses.sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
अदृष्टपूर्वं हृषितोऽस्मि दृष्ट्वा
भयेन च प्रव्यथितं मनो मे |
तदेव मे दर्शय देव रूपं
प्रसीद देवेश जगन्निवास || ४५ ||
verses.transliteration:
arjuna uvāca |
adṛṣṭapūrvaṃ hṛṣito'smi dṛṣṭvā
bhayena ca pravyathitaṃ mano me |
tadeva me darśaya deva rūpaṃ
prasīda deveśa jagannivāsa || 45 ||
verses.word_meanings: adṛṣṭa-pūrvam—what was never seen before; hṛṣitaḥ asmi—I am rejoiced; dṛṣṭvā—having seen; bhayena ca—and by fear; pravyathitam—is perturbed/shaken; manaḥ me—my mind; tat eva—that very; me—unto me; darśaya—reveal; deva—O Lord; rūpam—form; prasīda—be gracious; deva-īśa—O Lord of gods; jagat-nivāsa—O Abode of the Universe.
verses.translation: I am rejoiced to have seen what was never seen before, yet my mind is shaken with fear! Reveal to me, O Lord, that gentle, familiar form of Yours! Be gracious, O God of gods, O Abode of the Universe!
verses.meaning: Arjuna has experienced the awe of the infinite, but mortal consciousness cannot sustain such overwhelming cosmic intensity for long. He pleads to see Krishna's gentle, loving personal form once again.
verses.purport: Arjuna has experienced the awe of the infinite, but mortal consciousness cannot sustain such overwhelming cosmic intensity for long. He pleads to see Krishna's gentle, loving personal form once again.

verses.speaker: अर्जुन उवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
किरीटिनं गदिनं चक्रहस्त-
मिच्छामि त्वां द्रष्टुमहं तथैव |
तेनैव रूपेण चतुर्भुजेन
सहस्रबाहो भव विश्वमूर्ते || ४६ ||
verses.sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
किरीटिनं गदिनं चक्रहस्त-
मिच्छामि त्वां द्रष्टुमहं तथैव |
तेनैव रूपेण चतुर्भुजेन
सहस्रबाहो भव विश्वमूर्ते || ४६ ||
verses.transliteration:
arjuna uvāca |
kirīṭinaṃ gadinaṃ cakrahasta-
micchāmi tvāṃ draṣṭumahaṃ tathaiva |
tenaiva rūpeṇa caturbhujena
sahasrabāho bhava viśvamūrte || 46 ||
verses.word_meanings: kirīṭinam—with crown; gadinam—with mace; cakra-hastam—holding the discus in hand; icchāmi—I desire; tvām—You; draṣṭum—to see; aham—I; tathā eva—as before; tena eva rūpeṇa—in that very form; catuḥ-bhujena—four-armed; sahasra-bāho—O thousand-armed one; bhava—become; viśva-mūrte—O Universal Form.
verses.translation: I yearn to behold You as before, wearing a crown and holding the mace and discus in Your hand! O thousand-armed Universal Form, please assume once more Your four-armed divine form (Chaturbhuja)!
verses.meaning: Arjuna asks the thousand-armed cosmic form to withdraw into the majestic four-armed Vishnu form, adorned with conch, discus, mace, and lotus.
verses.purport: Arjuna asks the thousand-armed cosmic form to withdraw into the majestic four-armed Vishnu form, adorned with conch, discus, mace, and lotus.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
मया प्रसन्नेन तवार्जुनेदं
रूपं परं दर्शितमात्मयोगात् |
तेजोमयं विश्वमनन्तमाद्यं
यन्मे त्वदन्येन न दृष्टपूर्वम् || ४७ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
मया प्रसन्नेन तवार्जुनेदं
रूपं परं दर्शितमात्मयोगात् |
तेजोमयं विश्वमनन्तमाद्यं
यन्मे त्वदन्येन न दृष्टपूर्वम् || ४७ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
mayā prasannena tavārjunedaṃ
rūpaṃ paraṃ darśitamātmayogāt |
tejomayaṃ viśvamanantamādyaṃ
yanme tvadanyena na dṛṣṭapūrvam || 47 ||
verses.word_meanings: śrī-bhagavān uvāca—the Supreme Lord said; mayā prasannena—by Me being pleased with you; tava—unto you; arjuna—O Arjuna; idam—this; rūpam param—supreme cosmic form; darśitam—has been shown; ātma-yogāt—by My own mystic potency; tejomayam—radiant with light; viśvam—universal; anantam—infinite; ādyam—primeval; yat—which; me—of Mine; tvat-anyena—by anyone other than you; na dṛṣṭa-pūrvam—has never been seen before.
verses.translation: The Supreme Lord said: By My grace, O Arjuna, being pleased with you, I have revealed to you through My own divine power this supreme, radiant, infinite, primeval Universal Form of Mine, which no one other than you has ever seen before!
verses.meaning: Sri Krishna reassures Arjuna: This vision is not a wrathful curse, but the supreme badge of divine grace (Prasannena) granted because of Arjuna's unalloyed love.
verses.purport: Sri Krishna reassures Arjuna: This vision is not a wrathful curse, but the supreme badge of divine grace (Prasannena) granted because of Arjuna's unalloyed love.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
न वेदयज्ञाध्ययनैर्न दानै-
र्न च क्रियाभिर्न तपोभिरुग्रैः |
एवंरूपः शक्य अहं नृलोके
द्रष्टुं त्वदन्येन कुरुप्रवीर || ४८ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
न वेदयज्ञाध्ययनैर्न दानै-
र्न च क्रियाभिर्न तपोभिरुग्रैः |
एवंरूपः शक्य अहं नृलोके
द्रष्टुं त्वदन्येन कुरुप्रवीर || ४८ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
na vedayajñādhyayanairna dānai-
rna ca kriyābhirna tapobhirugraiḥ |
evaṃrūpaḥ śakya ahaṃ nṛloke
draṣṭuṃ tvadanyena kurupravīra || 48 ||
verses.word_meanings: na—neither; veda-yajña-adhyayanaiḥ—by the study of Vedas or sacrifices; na dānaiḥ—nor by charity; na ca kriyābhiḥ—nor by rituals; na tapobhiḥ ugraiḥ—nor by severe austerities; evam-rūpaḥ—in such a form; śakyaḥ aham—am I able; nṛ-loke—in the mortal world; draṣṭum—to be seen; tvat-anyena—by anyone other than you; kuru-pravīra—O hero of the Kurus.
verses.translation: Neither by the study of the Vedas and sacrifices, nor by charity, nor by ritualistic ceremonies, nor by severe austerities can I be seen in this cosmic form in the mortal world by anyone other than you, O hero of the Kurus!
verses.meaning: External Vedic scholarship, severe penances, and philanthropic deeds cannot force open the gates of divine vision; direct perception of God is granted purely through loving surrender.
verses.purport: External Vedic scholarship, severe penances, and philanthropic deeds cannot force open the gates of divine vision; direct perception of God is granted purely through loving surrender.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
मा ते व्यथा मा च विमूढभावो
दृष्ट्वा रूपं घोरमीदृङ्ममेदम् |
व्यपेतभीः प्रीतमनाः पुनस्त्वं
तदेव मे रूपमिदं प्रपश्य || ४९ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
मा ते व्यथा मा च विमूढभावो
दृष्ट्वा रूपं घोरमीदृङ्ममेदम् |
व्यपेतभीः प्रीतमनाः पुनस्त्वं
तदेव मे रूपमिदं प्रपश्य || ४९ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
mā te vyathā mā ca vimūḍhabhāvo
dṛṣṭvā rūpaṃ ghoramīdṛṅmamedam |
vyapetabhīḥ prītamanāḥ punastvaṃ
tadeva me rūpamidaṃ prapaśya || 49 ||
verses.word_meanings: mā—let there not be; te—unto you; vyathā—distress/fear; mā ca—nor; vimūḍha-bhāvaḥ—bewilderment; dṛṣṭvā—seeing; rūpam ghoram—fearsome form; īdṛk—such; mama idam—this of Mine; vyapeta-bhīḥ—freed from fear; prīta-manāḥ—with glad/peaceful heart; punaḥ—again; tvam—you; tat eva—that very; me—My; rūpam idam—this form; prapaśya—behold.
verses.translation: Let there be no fear, nor let your mind be bewildered by seeing this terrible form of Mine! Freed from fear, with a glad and peaceful heart, behold once again that familiar form of Mine!
verses.meaning: With tender compassion, Sri Krishna consoles His trembling friend and prepares to withdraw the terrifying vision of cosmic time to restore Arjuna's peaceful contemplation.
verses.purport: With tender compassion, Sri Krishna consoles His trembling friend and prepares to withdraw the terrifying vision of cosmic time to restore Arjuna's peaceful contemplation.

verses.speaker: सञ्जय उवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
सञ्जय उवाच |
इत्यर्जुनं वासुदेवस्तथोक्त्वा
स्वकं रूपं दर्शयामास भूयः |
आश्वासयामास च भीतमेनं
भूत्वा पुनः सौम्यवपुर्महात्मा || ५० ||
verses.sanskrit:
सञ्जय उवाच |
इत्यर्जुनं वासुदेवस्तथोक्त्वा
स्वकं रूपं दर्शयामास भूयः |
आश्वासयामास च भीतमेनं
भूत्वा पुनः सौम्यवपुर्महात्मा || ५० ||
verses.transliteration:
sañjaya uvāca |
ityarjunaṃ vāsudevastathoktvā
svakaṃ rūpaṃ darśayāmāsa bhūyaḥ |
āśvāsayāmāsa ca bhītamenaṃ
bhūtvā punaḥ saumyavapurmahātmā || 50 ||
verses.word_meanings: sañjayaḥ uvāca—Sanjaya said; iti—thus; arjunam—unto Arjuna; vāsudevaḥ—Vasudeva (Krishna); tathā uktvā—having spoken so; svakam rūpam—His own familiar form; darśayāmāsa—showed; bhūyaḥ—again; āśvāsayāmāsa ca—and consoled; bhītam enam—the terrified Arjuna; bhūtvā—becoming; punaḥ—again; saumya-vapuḥ—of gentle/graceful form; mahātmā—the Great Soul.
verses.translation: Sanjaya said: Having spoken thus to Arjuna, Vasudeva (Krishna) showed His own familiar form again; and assuming once more His gentle and graceful human form (Saumya-vapus), the Great Soul consoled the terrified Arjuna.
verses.meaning: The ultimate transformation: The all-devouring cosmic fire condenses back into the sweetest, most enchanting two-armed personal form (Saumya-vapus) of Sri Krishna, dispelling all fear.
verses.purport: The ultimate transformation: The all-devouring cosmic fire condenses back into the sweetest, most enchanting two-armed personal form (Saumya-vapus) of Sri Krishna, dispelling all fear.

verses.speaker: अर्जुन उवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
दृष्ट्वेदं मानुषं रूपं तव सौम्यं जनार्दन |
इदानीमस्मि संवृत्तः सचेताः प्रकृतिं गतः || ५१ ||
verses.sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
दृष्ट्वेदं मानुषं रूपं तव सौम्यं जनार्दन |
इदानीमस्मि संवृत्तः सचेताः प्रकृतिं गतः || ५१ ||
verses.transliteration:
arjuna uvāca |
dṛṣṭvedaṃ mānuṣaṃ rūpaṃ tava saumyaṃ janārdana |
idānīmasmi saṃvṛttaḥ sacetāḥ prakṛtiṃ gataḥ || 51 ||
verses.word_meanings: arjunaḥ uvāca—Arjuna said; dṛṣṭvā—beholding; idam—this; mānuṣam rūpam—human form; tava—Your; saumyam—gentle/beautiful; janārdana—O Janardana; idānīm—now; asmi saṃvṛttaḥ—I have become; sacetāḥ—composed in mind; prakṛtim gataḥ—restored to my normal nature.
verses.translation: Arjuna said: Beholding this gentle human form of Yours, O Janardana, I have now become composed in mind and restored to my normal self.
verses.meaning: Arjuna breathes a sigh of relief. The terrifying grandeur of the cosmos gives way to the intimate, comforting presence of the loving Lord.
verses.purport: Arjuna breathes a sigh of relief. The terrifying grandeur of the cosmos gives way to the intimate, comforting presence of the loving Lord.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
सुदुर्दर्शमिदं रूपं दृष्टवानसि यन्मम |
देवा अप्यस्य रूपस्य नित्यं दर्शनकाङ्क्षिणः || ५२ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
सुदुर्दर्शमिदं रूपं दृष्टवानसि यन्मम |
देवा अप्यस्य रूपस्य नित्यं दर्शनकाङ्क्षिणः || ५२ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
sudurdarśamidaṃ rūpaṃ dṛṣṭavānasi yanmama |
devā apyasya rūpasya nityaṃ darśanakāṅkṣiṇaḥ || 52 ||
verses.word_meanings: śrī-bhagavān uvāca—the Supreme Lord said; su-durdarśam—extremely rare and difficult to see; idam—this; rūpam—form; dṛṣṭavān asi—you have seen; yat mama—which of Mine; devāḥ api—even the celestial gods; asya rūpasya—of this form; nityam—always; darśana-kāṅkṣiṇaḥ—longing for the vision.
verses.translation: The Supreme Lord said: This form of Mine which you have seen is exceedingly difficult to behold. Even the celestial gods are ever longing to catch a glimpse of this divine form!
verses.meaning: Sri Krishna emphasizes the priceless nature of the revelation: Even heavenly deities perform penances for millions of years yearning to behold this transcendental reality.
verses.purport: Sri Krishna emphasizes the priceless nature of the revelation: Even heavenly deities perform penances for millions of years yearning to behold this transcendental reality.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
नाहं वेदैर्न तपसा न दानेन न चेज्यया |
शक्य एवंविधो द्रष्टुं दृष्टवानसि मां यथा || ५३ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
नाहं वेदैर्न तपसा न दानेन न चेज्यया |
शक्य एवंविधो द्रष्टुं दृष्टवानसि मां यथा || ५३ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
nāhaṃ vedairna tapasā na dānena na cejyayā |
śakya evaṃvidho draṣṭuṃ dṛṣṭavānasi māṃ yathā || 53 ||
verses.word_meanings: na aham—not I; vedaiḥ—by the Vedas; na tapasā—nor by austerity; na dānena—nor by gifts/charity; na ca ijyayā—nor by sacrifice/worship; śakyaḥ—possible; evaṃ-vidhaḥ—in this manner; draṣṭum—to be seen; dṛṣṭavān asi—have seen; mām—Me; yathā—as.
verses.translation: Neither by the Vedas, nor by austerities, nor by charity, nor by ritual sacrifices can I be seen in this form as you have seen Me.
verses.meaning: The Lord repeats the supreme spiritual truth: Spiritual realization cannot be bought or earned through mechanical piety; it yields only to love.
verses.purport: The Lord repeats the supreme spiritual truth: Spiritual realization cannot be bought or earned through mechanical piety; it yields only to love.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
भक्त्या त्वनन्यया शक्य अहमेवंविधोऽर्जुन |
ज्ञातुं द्रष्टुं च तत्त्वेन प्रवेष्टुं च परन्तप || ५४ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
भक्त्या त्वनन्यया शक्य अहमेवंविधोऽर्जुन |
ज्ञातुं द्रष्टुं च तत्त्वेन प्रवेष्टुं च परन्तप || ५४ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
bhaktyā tvananyayā śakya ahamevaṃvidho'rjuna |
jñātuṃ draṣṭuṃ ca tattvena praveṣṭuṃ ca parantapa || 54 ||
verses.word_meanings: bhaktyā—by devotion; tu—but; ananyayā—by exclusive/unalloyed; śakyaḥ—possible; aham—I am; evaṃ-vidhaḥ—in this way; arjuna—O Arjuna; jñātum—to be known; draṣṭum ca—and to be seen; tattvena—in truth/essence; praveṣṭum ca—and to be entered into; parantapa—O chastiser of foes.
verses.translation: Only by undivided, unalloyed devotion (Ananya Bhakti), O Arjuna, can I be known in truth, directly seen, and entered into, O scorcher of foes!
verses.meaning: The master key of the Bhagavad Gita: Bhakti (pure, undivided love) alone has the power to know God in truth (Jñātum), to behold Him face-to-face (Draṣṭum), and to merge into eternal communion with Him (Praveṣṭum).
verses.purport: The master key of the Bhagavad Gita: Bhakti (pure, undivided love) alone has the power to know God in truth (Jñātum), to behold Him face-to-face (Draṣṭum), and to merge into eternal communion with Him (Praveṣṭum).

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
मत्कर्मकृन्मत्परमो मद्भक्तः सङ्गवर्जितः |
निर्वैरः सर्वभूतेषु यः स मामेति पाण्डव || ५५ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
मत्कर्मकृन्मत्परमो मद्भक्तः सङ्गवर्जितः |
निर्वैरः सर्वभूतेषु यः स मामेति पाण्डव || ५५ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
matkarmakṛnmatparamo madbhaktaḥ saṅgavarjitaḥ |
nirvairaḥ sarvabhūteṣu yaḥ sa māmeti pāṇḍava || 55 ||
verses.word_meanings: mat-karma-kṛt—one who acts for Me/dedicates all actions to Me; mat-paramaḥ—making Me the Supreme Goal; mad-bhaktaḥ—My loving devotee; saṅga-varjitaḥ—free from worldly attachments; nirvairaḥ—free from enmity/malice; sarva-bhūteṣu—towards all living beings; yaḥ—whoever; saḥ—he; mām—unto Me; eti—comes; pāṇḍava—O son of Pandu.
verses.translation: He who dedicates all actions unto Me, who regards Me as the Supreme Goal, who is devoted to Me, free from material attachments, and devoid of enmity toward all living beings—he certainly comes unto Me, O son of Pandu!
verses.meaning: The glorious grand conclusion of Chapter 11 (designated by Acharya Shankara and Ramanuja as the quintessence of the entire Gita). Sri Krishna outlines the five golden principles of spiritual liberation: 1) Mat-karma-krit (dedicating all works to God), 2) Mat-parama (holding God as supreme refuge), 3) Mad-bhakta (loving devotion), 4) Sanga-varjita (freedom from worldly clinging), and 5) Nirvaira (universal compassion without malice toward any creature). One who lives thus attains eternal union with the Supreme.
verses.purport: The glorious grand conclusion of Chapter 11 (designated by Acharya Shankara and Ramanuja as the quintessence of the entire Gita).
